title: Midday Brief — Fri 27 Nov

stories.board: Supreme Court keeps Quebec's religious symbols law
stories.headline: Canada's top court mostly upholds Quebec's Bill 21
stories.what: The Supreme Court kept the ban on religious symbols, like a kippah, hijab or turban, for teachers, judges and police. It was close: 4 judges to 3. One part, a ban on face coverings for Quebec lawmakers, was struck down.
stories.why: The court said provinces may use the notwithstanding clause (a rule to override some Charter rights) and courts cannot second-guess it, though some judges said courts should still speak up.
stories.sides: Quebec defended the law as protecting a neutral state; Muslim groups, school boards and rights groups called the ruling a blow to minorities and vow to keep fighting.

sources.name: CTV News / Canadian Press via CP24
Toronto Sun via Yahoo News Canada

stories.board: Israel's hospitals on alert for cyberattack
stories.headline: Israel warns hospitals of a possible big cyberattack
stories.what: Israel's Health Ministry warned hospitals that a coordinated cyberattack (computer hackers breaking into systems) may be coming. Maccabi, a big health provider, blocked access from outside Israel until at least Sunday.
stories.why: Hospitals need their computers for patient care, so an attack could slow treatment.
stories.sides: No major disagreement. The ministry has not said who might be behind it.

quick_hits: Israel: Gadi Eisenkot's side wants to swear in a new government next week, but still needs 61 seats and is pushing the Shas party to join (Ynetnews).
US stocks rose in a short Black Friday trading day that ends at 1 p.m., led by chip makers, after a rough week.
big_picture: Canada's top court said elected lawmakers get the final word on Bill 21, by just one vote.
